 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death one (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3429/2023 Sri.Nagendra.K.C S/o late Chikka Muniyappa, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 14.05.2022 at about 08.45 p.m the deceased Nagendra.K.C was riding the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-50-EA-0364 towards Platinum City to Basaveshwara Bus Stop,
at that time the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-04-C-2188 driven in rash and negligent manner, with high speed by its driver and dashed against the Motor Cycle.
Due to this, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Ravi Kirloskar hospital, Peenya, Bengaluru and he was shifted to People Tree hospital, Goragunte Palya.

Even after best medical treatment,
he was passed away on 21.05.2022, leaving behind the petitioners herein as his legal heirs.
The petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation, obsequies and last rites.
Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was working as Field Executive at M/s Jumbotail and earning more than Rs.30,000/- p.m.

The petitioner No.1 is the mother, petitioner No.2 is the step mother and petitioner No.3 is the sister of the deceased have lost (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3429/2023 their sole earning member of the family and deprived of love and affection and put to great hardship and financial difficulties and suffering from mental shock, mental agony due to death of deceased.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Auto rickshaw and in this regard the Peenya Police have registered a case against driver of the offending Auto rickshaw in Crime No.86/2022 for the offence punishable U/Sec 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC and Sec.146 r/w 196 of M.V. Act.

Therefore, the respondents No.1 and 2 being the owners and respondent No.3 being the driver of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.

2 03.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 remained absent and hence, they were placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.3 has appeared before the tribunal through his counsel and filed objection statement.

04. The respondent No.3 in his objection statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and admits the accident date and further denied name, age, occupation and income of deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners and dependency of the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.3429/2023 petitioners and manner and mode of accident and involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and contended that he was busy in shifting the injured person to the hosptial for treatment and he could not lodge the complaint in person on the same day as the injured was in critical condition and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased himself, but the Charge sheet is filed against him and he is only accused to this accident and not an owner of the said Auto rickshaw and he had valid licence to drive the Auto rickshaw and they are not at fault and hence, he is not liable to pay compensation and pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.3 with costs.
05.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Nagendra K.C S/o late Chikka Muniyappa?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Nagendra K.C S/o late Chikka Muniyappa, was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 14.05.2022 at about 8.45 p.m, Triveni (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.3429/2023 Turbains Factory Junction, Peenya Pipeline Road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of Auto rikshaw bearing registration No.KA-04-C-2188 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?
06. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 and closed her side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the counsel for the respondent No.3 submits no oral evidence.
Hence, the respondent No.3 evidence is taken as nil and closed its side evidence.
08. Heard both sides.

3

09. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 :
Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following:-
 (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3429/2023  REASONS 10.

Issue No.1:- Petitioner No.1 in her affidavit stated that, she is the mother,
petitioner No.2 is the step mother and petitioner No.3 is the sister of the deceased.
To prove the said Issue No.1, petitioners have produced Family tree, notarized copies of Aadhaar cards and driving licence of the deceased as per Ex.P.13 to 18.
In her cross-examination PW.1 has stated that her husband had two wives, herself and another is Jayamma and petitioner No.3 is her daughter.

So on perusal of these documents it is true that the petitioners No.1 and 2 being the mother and step mother and petitioner No.3 being the sister of the deceased and they are the legal representatives of the deceased.

However, it is elicit from the mouth of PW.1 that the petitioner No.3 is married before 10 years and is living separately with her matrimonial home and her expenses are incurred by her husband, witness volunteers that now a days her son was looking after her.
But in this regard the petitioners have not produced any documents and hence she is not the dependent on the earnings of the deceased and she is depending on the earnings of her husband.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:- PW.1 filed affidavit by stating that, due to the negligence of driver of the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-04-C-2188 accident took place and deceased died in the accident.

But in her cross-examination she has stated that she has seen the accident spot and it is a big road and the vehicles are coming on four way and admits that the vehicles are coming slowly on the said road and denied to the suggestion that on the date of accident her son was riding the Motor Cycle in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Auto rickshaw, due to this the Auto rickshaw was toppled and the accident occurred due to negligence of her son and not by driver of Auto rickshaw.
In Ravi Kirloskar hospital the doctor have not treated her son by stating that her son was consumed alcohol and her son had driving licence to ride bike.
On perusal of the exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Peenya Traffic Police in Crime No.86/2022 against driver of the Auto rickshaw for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent driving of Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA- 04-C-2188 by its driver the accident took place.
is the Charge sheet shows that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has filed Charge Jayalakshmamma vs Sundar.P

on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191579500/
4 sheet against driver of the offending Auto rickshaw as A1 and owner/respondent No.1 of the offending Auto rickshaw as A2 for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337, 304-A of IPC and Sec.146, 196, 56 and 192 of MV Act for the reasons that the accused/respondent No.1 was absconding and he had no valid insurance and fitness certificate as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.4 is IMV report which shows involvement of both vehicles in the accident.
Ex.P.5 is Spot Mahazar with Sketch showing the place of accident near Triveni Turbains Factory Junction, on Platinum City Road towards Basaveshwara Bus Stop, Peenya, Bengaluru, is not disputed.
Ex.P.6 is the Inquest panchanama of the deceased which is not disputed the death has taken place.
Ex.P.7 is the PM report showing cause of death is due to coma as a result of head injury sustained.
Ex.P.12 is Death certificate of the deceased.

These documents clearly goes to show that, due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Auto rickshaw, the accident took place and deceased sustained injuries and died during treatment.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.

(SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.3429/2023 12. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Nagendra.K.C, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was working as Field Executive at M/s Jumbotail and earning more than Rs.30,000/- p.m and have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation, obsequies and last rites.
On account of untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great mental shock and agony and lost love and affection and financial support.
13. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any school records, SSLC marks card or birth certificate of the deceased to show date of birth of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.17 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.19 Driving licence of deceased.

Eventhough the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age, but in the absence of other evidence, the said documents can be relied upon and according to which his date of birth is mentioned as 16.06.1997.
The alleged accident occurred on 14.05.2022.
Hence, it (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3429/2023 appears that as on the date of accident the deceased is aged 25 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 25 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is 18.
14.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove the avocation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.9 Experience letter, Ex.P.10 Pay slips for the month of February, March, April 2022 which shows that he was drawing gross salary of Rs.20,686/- and Ex.P.11 Statement of bank account of deceased which shows salary was credited to the account of the deceased.
But the petitioners have not examined the employer and author of the said documents to prove income of the deceased.

Therefore, in the absence of rebuttal evidence regarding the avocation and income of the deceased,
this tribunal has relied upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru, the notional income as per the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/-.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Therefore,
Jayalakshmamma vs Sundar.P on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191579500/
5

this tribunal has assessed the notional income of the (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.3429/2023 deceased at Rs.15,500/- p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
15.
In the instant case, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 being the mother and petitioner No.2 being the step mother of deceased are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.
No evidence on record to show that the petitioner No.3 is also depending on the earnings of the deceased.

It is also evident that the deceased in the present case was a bachelor and hence 50% of the income has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
16.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since deceased was aged about 25 years and was self employee at the time of accident, 40% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (15,500 +
6,200) = Rs.21,700/-.

Since the deceased was a bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (21,700 - 10,850) = (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.3429/2023 Rs.10,850/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.10,850/-.
As the deceased was aged about 25 years, the multiplier of 18 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.23,43,600/- (Rs.10,850 x 12 x 18) towards loss of dependency.

17. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, in the head of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
18. The claimants No.1 and 2 are the mother and step mother of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 and 2 would be entitled for Rs.48,400/- each towards loss of filial consortium.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioner No.3 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 50% of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Dependency (After 23,43,600-00 deducting 50% of the income towards personal and living expenses)
Jayalakshmamma vs Sundar.P on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191579500/
6 2. Loss of filial consortium 96,800-00 (For petitioner Nos.1 and 2)
3. Loss of love and affection 40,000-00 (For petitioner No.3)
4. Loss of estate 19,500-00 5.
Funeral expenses and 19,500-00 transportation of dead body Total 25,19,400-00 19.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,19,400/-
with (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3429/2023 interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
20.
Regarding liability:- Despite service of notice, respondents No.1 and 2 remained absent and placed exparte.

Though the respondent No.3 has appeared and filed written statement and contest the matter, but has not lead any evidence to prove that due to rash and negligent riding of deceased,
the accident took place and it also appears in the Charge sheet that the offending Auto rickshaw had no insurance and fitness certificate as on the date of accident.

Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount to the petitioners within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit and respondent No.3 being the driver is exonarated from the payment of compensation.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the Affirmative.
21. Issue No.4:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
 (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.3429/2023  ORDER  The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,19,400/- (Rupees Twenty five lakhs nineteen thousand and four hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2, shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner No.1 being the mother and petitioner No.2 being the step mother were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 50-50, in the award amount together with interest.

Jayalakshmamma vs Sundar.P on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191579500/
7
The petitioner No.3 being married daughter is entitled for Rs.40,000/- (towards loss of love and affection) in the award amount together with interest.

The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.3429/2023 in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The petitioner No.3 is entitled to get release her entire share in the award amount through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining the bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
